body:
# Independent complete audit of the symmetric planar chain theorem


correction required. This is not a verdict on unrestricted (OC).

The audited main statement is
`candidate 0f11bff1d492f9c2`.
I read its full dependency graph, independently checked the geometric
and scalar interfaces, and reran the relevant exact verifiers. In
particular I read:

- `candidate 42889f299dc055c9`;
- `candidate 58714b1fac606069`;
- `candidate ff51b2f45de7ad0e`;
- `candidate 9c420d2e51075e2c`;
- `candidate f1d41e47743392b2`;
- `candidate aae24573a37976a6`;
- its functional input
  `candidate dafd411c026c302c`, together
  with the existing independent weighted-tail and three-homothetic audits.

## 1. Exact scope, measure, source, and candidate

The theorem concerns one integer coordinate and two continuous
coordinates, with a symmetric concave radius sequence at consecutive
integer bases. The fibers are the actual planar triangles r_h T.
The candidate y=(0,R/3,R/3) is uniquely specified and lies in the
interior of the positive peak triangle: both coordinates are positive
and their sum is 2R/3<R. It is never rounded or averaged across bases.

For m>=1, the displayed linear interpolation r(z) is concave,
nonnegative, and positive near zero. Its hypograph description with
x_1,x_2>=0 is compact, convex, and has interior in R^3. Evaluation at
the integer bases gives precisely the prescribed fibers. Their finite
union has Hausdorff dimension 2, positive finite H_2 mass, and

    H_2(S)=V sum_h r_h^2=VM.

The sum identity is ordinary countable additivity of Hausdorff measure
on the finitely many disjoint vertical planes, whose induced metric
is the standard Euclidean metric on each R^2 fiber.

The main theorem assumes positive displayed radii. Additional zero-area
fibers contribute no H_2 mass and cannot change its cap inequalities.
If symmetric endpoint radii equal zero, one can simply remove those
zero-area endpoints: the remaining positive block is still symmetric
and concave, and its peak and all H_2 masses are unchanged. No limit
or assumption of null mass at a positive-dimensional fiber is needed.
This does not create an assertion about intersections with intrinsic
dimension less than 2; the main note explicitly declines that scope.

## 2. Every original closed ambient halfspace is retained

Moving a containing halfspace parallel until its boundary passes
through y replaces it by a subset. For a nonzero continuous normal,
the positive-normal reduction uses an actual volume-preserving
barycentric involution on each triangle. Its centroid fixation and
margin identity are exact. Because r_h<=R, the affine majorant at
the peak has slope zero, and the single replacement affine margin
is no larger than the swapped original margin on EVERY fiber.
The resulting replacement is an actual ambient halfspace through y,
with nonnegative nonzero continuous normal and no larger cap mass
on any original fiber. The fiberwise swaps are not represented as
one lattice-preserving ambient map; the separate ambient margin is
what justifies the replacement.

Purely vertical caps are not discarded. The source proof's finite
large-tilt replacement retains full originally positive-side fibers,
excludes negative-side fibers, and cuts subsets of the whole boundary
fibers. In this symmetric chain one could also directly use the
at-least-half-total-mass bound for a vertical through-point cap.

After positive normalization and a continuous coordinate exchange,
the normal is (a,1-a), 1/2<=a<=1. There remains exactly ONE real
integer tilt beta in every cap. Every nonvertical boundary cuts
each positive triangle in a line or a supporting face and has zero
area. Vertical boundaries containing an entire fiber count that
fiber in full. Thus closed-halfspace boundary mass has been handled
in the appropriate separate cases, not erased by an open-cap change.

The normal reduction is at the actual own centroid and is valid
there; no assertion for arbitrary candidates is used. Attainment of
a minimizing cap is not needed for the theorem's universal bounds,
but the cited finite-tilt compactness proof also correctly supplies it.

## 3. Exact tails, pair floors, and the endpoint sectors

The triangular tail formula agrees at both proper-cut joins, including
the first derivative. For 1/2<a<1 its pair minimization exhausts all
pieces: two lower pieces, two upper pieces, a straddling pair, a
full cap, and an empty cap. The only proper straddling minimum is
the displayed stationary one when the normalized middle height
exceeds 1/2 and the normalized threshold lies between 1/2 and that
height. At piece endpoints the first derivatives match, so no
additional minimum is omitted. The degenerate height cases a=1/2
and a=1 are computed directly in their one-piece formulas.

For a>=2/3 the zero-shift pair value is at most one full fiber.
For the peak radius this comparison simplifies to
2(a-1/3)^2<=a(2a-1), exactly a>=2/3; smaller radii only decrease
the normalized upper-tail value. There is no smaller straddling
minimum. Thus every pair's lower value occurs at the SAME beta=0,
which proves the exact high-sector sum without a compatibility gap.
The independently audited quadratic truncation theorem gives its
factor at least 1/4, strictly exceeding 2/9.

At a=1/2 the exact pair floor is 8t(r-2t)_+, t=R/3; the own
contribution is 5R^2/9. The scalar hinge proof keeps the finite
trapezoid error -sum delta_i^2/6. Its inverse-radius density is
a finite nondecreasing step function; initial plateaus can occur
only at the maximum and are counted separately. The primitive
sign and endpoint minimization produce exactly -13/27 after
normalization. Restoring the own term yields the stated surplus
R^2/243 over (2/9)M. This is valid for every shared tilt because
only lower pair floors are being summed; simultaneous attainment
is not presumed in this sector.

## 4. Intermediate geometry and the exact finite correction

For 1/2<a<2/3, the pair floor is exactly 2k_a(r), and the actual
own cap is k_a(1)+g. Hence the lower budget g+sum k_a(r_h) counts
the own fiber exactly once and preserves its positive surplus.

The ratio k_a(r)/r^2 is nondecreasing on every piece and across
the joins. On the upper piece its derivative has the required
sign because 2/(3r)-a>0 for r<=1 and a<2/3. The identity
lambda=3 integral_0^1 k_a gives a single sign change of
k_a(r)-lambda r^2 and nonnegative integrals over all upper
intervals. The finite inverse-radius step representation therefore
proves the polygonal comparison, including its plateau contribution.

The correction does not replace sampled mass with an integral.
Writing H=(r-rho)_+^2, the function k_a+B H is convex with
continuous derivative. The error kernel identity is valid by two
integrations by parts; the second derivative of H is piecewise
constant and has no derivative-jump atom. Its kernel increases
when either interval endpoint is expanded outward, so the sum
of all cell errors is bounded by the single [b,1] error E_a(b).
Both formulas for E agree at b=rho; b=1 uses the zero first branch.

The exact identities

    sum k_a(r_h)=2T_k+k_a(b),
    M=2 integral r(z)^2 dz+b^2+(1/3)sum delta_i^2

and sum delta_i^2<=(1-b)^2 give precisely the displayed lower
bound with -2B E_a(b). Every discrete error and endpoint term
has the correct factor of two.

The second cap budget follows from the pointwise hinge comparison
and the already proved square-truncation theorem. Its coefficient
v obeys v-2/9=(12a^2-9a+1)/(27a^2), so alpha is exactly the
upper root and a>=alpha is settled directly. For a<alpha, a
strictly bad cap forces M>M0 from its own fiber and M>M1 from
g+vM. For m>=2, concavity gives r_1>=(1+b)/2 and monotonicity
gives r_2>=b, yielding M>=M2(b). Since lambda-2/9>0, substituting
the maximum of these three lower thresholds in the proposed
deficit is in the correct direction. The proof uses the strict
failure assumption only where it is explicitly stated.

## 5. Scalar closure is a finite algebraic proof on the full domain

I checked the branch maps, denominator signs, monotonicity in M,
rectangle coverage, and the upper-a replacement M1>6 in the exact
certificate. The Bernstein coefficient identity is proved there
by the binomial theorem. Nonnegative coefficients therefore establish
positivity on entire rectangles; this is not a finite point screen.

The first six rectangles cover all three b branches for
1/2<a<=3/5. The last three cover 3/5<=a<alpha, where M1>6 is
separately established. Values a=1/2 and a=2/3 on the polynomial
rectangles are used only for certification of the canceled
polynomials, not as evaluations of singular original rational
expressions. The actual scalar statement uses the appropriate
open a interval. The b=0, b=1, b=c, and b=rho boundaries are
all included by the matching branch definitions.

The exact rational certificate rerun reproduced all nine table minima
and the separate 1/125 lower Bernstein coefficient for M1>6. Thus
the scalar dependency closes the entire remaining real parameter
domain. It leaves no numerical or conjectural sublemma in this
restricted chain proof.

## 6. Small lengths and the chosen center

For m=0 ordinary planar Gruenbaum at the triangle centroid gives
4V/9, more than the required 2V/9 after R=1 normalization.

For m=1 the actual three bodies are r_1 T, R T, r_1 T, with
midpoint inclusion r_1 T subset R T. They are homothets of the
centroid-zero body K=T-g_T with their genuine translations retained.
An endpoint can never be half-mass heavy because R>0. If
R^2>=2r_1^2, the middle centroid's own ordinary bound alone pays
the target. Otherwise the cited three-homothetic theorem explicitly
chooses the middle ordinary centroid. In either case its selected
point is exactly y; the theorem is not merely an existence statement
with a possibly different base or continuous coordinate.

I checked that theorem's cap accounting: its translated retained
endpoint is an actual subset, its additional middle contribution
is computed at the SAME middle centroid by an exact concentric
homothety identity, and its scalar trimming inequality is applied
only with a positive required bracket. Vertical caps retain the
whole middle fiber. The measurable-subset three-tail input is
already proved and independently audited; its ordinary localization
argument uses a shifted central threshold to exclude the spurious
Dirac case. No OC theorem or equivalent mixed-integer selection
principle is invoked in this dependency.

## 7. Constants, transformations, limits, and conclusion

All masses in the geometric scalar formulas are divided by V and
normalized by R^2 exactly once. Restoring the continuous scaling
gives the absolute target (2/9)VM=2^(-1)gamma_2 H_2(S).
The allowed maps have integer base epsilon z+j and an invertible
continuous affine part A x+bz+c. They preserve the mixed lattice,
send closed halfspaces bijectively to closed halfspaces, multiply
each fiber area by |det A|, and send y to its actual image in S.
No general affine change of integer coordinates is used.

There is no rational approximation, escaping center, exchange of a
maximum with a limit, or omitted intrinsic boundary case inside the
stated theorem. The proof bounds every original cap at one fixed
actual point. It proves all lengths and every ambient halfspace
for this symmetric planar common-vertex family only.

Reproduced checks:

- positive-normal reduction: 1,944 exact swap/margin checks, saturation,
  and finite replacement vertices;
- shared-tilt geometry: 9,149 exact pair, chamber, sequence, sector,
  and lattice-phase checks;
- quadratic truncation: 28,578 exact checks;
- three-homothetic theorem: 3,534 scalar checks, 721 radius cases,
  6,400 actual triangular caps, and vertical caps;
- scalar closure: all nine exact Bernstein certificates and the
  separate six-bound certificate.

These computations supplement the mathematical dependency audit;
they are not substitutes for the all-parameter arguments above.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
